scope: Empire State Building, New York City
title: Empire State Building
blurb: The 102 story Art Deco skyscraper at 350 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, the world's tallest building from 1931 to 1970. Its Indiana limestone tower, twin observatories, and dirigible mooring mast made it a global icon.

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: Concrete footings and bedrock anchors below street level, carrying the 365,000 short ton weight of the building.

systems.name: Base
systems.description: The five story Indiana limestone base filling the whole city block, with the Fifth Avenue entrance and the storefronts.

systems.name: Shaft
systems.description: The 81 story setback shaft between the base and the crown, clad in limestone with steel framed windows.

systems.name: Setback terraces
systems.description: Open terraces at each setback level, stepping the tower back as required by the 1916 Zoning Resolution.

systems.name: Observatories
systems.description: The 80th, 86th, and 102nd floor observatories, visited by about four million tourists a year.

systems.name: Mast
systems.description: The mooring mast and pinnacle above the 102nd floor, first planned for docking dirigibles and now carrying broadcast antennas.

systems.name: Crown lighting
systems.description: Architectural lighting for the crown, from the 1964 Worlds Fair floodlights to the 1,200 LED fixtures of 2012.

systems.name: Lobby
systems.description: The three story Art Deco lobby interior, with marble, terrazzo, bronze motifs, and a sky mural.

systems.name: Steel frame
systems.description: The riveted steel frame and the central utility core, revealed when the model is exploded.

systems.name: Elevators
systems.description: The 73 elevators in vertical banks in the central core, with express shuttles to the observatories.

explanations.foundation footings: Concrete footings spread the 365,000 short ton weight of the building onto the rock below. Depth and spread shown here are schematic.
explanations.bedrock anchor slab: A rock anchor slab ties the footings to Manhattan bedrock. Shown schematically below street level.
explanations.five story limestone base: The five story base occupies the entire lot, with the 81 story shaft set back sharply above it. The facade is clad in Indiana limestone panels that give the building its signature blonde color.
explanations.fifth avenue entrance: The main entrance sits at the center of the Fifth Avenue elevation: three sets of metal doors flanked by molded piers.
explanations.fifth avenue transom window: A triple height transom window with geometric patterns sits above the main entrance.
explanations.empire state golden letters: Golden letters spelling Empire State sit above the fifth floor windows.
explanations.entrance eagles: A pair of sculpted concrete eagles crowns the molded piers that flank the Fifth Avenue entrance.
explanations.first floor granite storefronts: The first floor storefronts use aluminum framed doors and windows set within black granite cladding.
explanations.33rd street west entrance: One of two entrances on 33rd Street, carrying a modernistic stainless steel canopy. The triple windows above the secondary entrances are less elaborate than those on Fifth Avenue.
explanations.33rd street east entrance: One of two entrances on 33rd Street, carrying a modernistic stainless steel canopy. The triple windows above the secondary entrances are less elaborate than those on Fifth Avenue.
explanations.34th street west entrance: One of two entrances on 34th Street, carrying a modernistic stainless steel canopy. The triple windows above the secondary entrances are less elaborate than those on Fifth Avenue.
explanations.34th street east entrance: One of two entrances on 34th Street, carrying a modernistic stainless steel canopy. The triple windows above the secondary entrances are less elaborate than those on Fifth Avenue.
explanations.base cornice: The fifth story is topped by a horizontal stone sill, marking the top of the five story base.
explanations.art deco crown core: The 16 story, 200 foot (61 m) metal crown above the 86th floor. The spire does not contain intermediate levels and is used mostly for mechanical purposes.
explanations.crown window bands: Schematic window bands on the crown tower.
explanations.crown setback ledges: The stepped ledges of the Art Deco crown profile. The stepping is schematic.
explanations.crown mechanical floors: Mechanical floors between the 87th and 101st floors, inside the crown. The elevator between the 86th and 102nd floors also serves employees reaching these floors. Layout is schematic.
explanations.86th floor open air deck: The 86th floor observatory pairs an enclosed viewing gallery with this open air outdoor viewing area at 1,050 feet (320 m), so it can stay open 365 days a year regardless of the weather.
explanations.86th floor enclosed gallery: The enclosed viewing gallery of the 86th floor observatory.
explanations.86th floor telescope stands: Viewing stands on the 86th floor deck. Fixture positions are schematic.
explanations.102nd floor glass enclosure: The 102nd floor observatory is completely enclosed and much smaller than the 86th. It was redesigned in 2019 with floor to ceiling windows.
explanations.102nd floor observation roof: The roof of the 102nd floor observatory at the 1,250 foot (381 m) roof height.
explanations.80th floor indoor observatory: An indoor observatory on the 80th floor opened in 2019 with exhibits and hands on displays about the building history.
explanations.80th floor skyline mural: A mural of the skyline drawn by British artist Stephen Wiltshire, installed in the 80th floor observatory. Shown schematically.
explanations.observatory entrance, 20 west 34th stree: Visitors to the observatories enter at 20 West 34th Street. Before August 2018 they entered through the Fifth Avenue lobby.
explanations.mooring mast, tier 1: The lowest stacked tier of the mooring mast above the 102nd story. The mast was first planned for docking zeppelins and other airships, but the plan was abandoned because high winds made docking impossible. Tier divisions are schematic.
explanations.mooring mast, tier 2: The middle stacked tier of the mooring mast. The mast holds a 158 foot hollow steel shaft fitted with elevators and utilities. Tier divisions are schematic.
explanations.mooring mast, tier 3: The upper stacked tier of the mooring mast. As constructed, the mast contains four rectangular tiers topped by a cylindrical shaft with a conical pinnacle. Tier divisions are schematic.
explanations.mooring mast base collar: Base collar where the mooring mast meets the 102nd story. Shown schematically.
explanations.dirigible docking ring: Schematic docking ring at the equivalent of the 106th floor, where airships would have been moored to the spire. No dirigible ever docked here.
explanations.103rd floor balcony: The 103rd floor, originally planned as the airship docking station, now contains electrical equipment and has an exterior balcony. Shown schematically.
explanations.broadcast antenna whips: Broadcast antenna whips on the pinnacle. Much of the 203 foot (61.9 m) pinnacle is covered by broadcast antennas. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.broadcast panel antennas: Broadcast panel antennas on the pinnacle. A dedicated 200 foot broadcast tower was completed in 1953. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.fm antenna ring, 1965: A separate set of FM antennae built in 1965, ringing the 103rd floor observation area as a master antenna. Shown schematically.
explanations.lightning rod: A lightning rod surmounts the pinnacle at the very top, reaching the 1,454 foot (443.2 m) tip.
explanations.original rooftop searchlights: The building was originally equipped with white searchlights at the top. They were first used in November 1932 when they lit up to signal the Roosevelt victory over Hoover in the presidential election.
explanations.freedom lights, 1956: Four "Freedom Lights" installed in 1956, replacing the original searchlights.
explanations.72nd floor floodlights: Flood lights were added on the 72nd floor in February 1964 to illuminate the top of the building at night so it could be seen from the Worlds Fair later that year.
explanations.mast and deck light rings: Schematic light rings on the mooring mast and the 86th floor deck.
explanations.led crown fixtures: In 2012, four hundred metal halide lamps and floodlights were replaced with 1,200 computer controlled LED fixtures, raising the available colors from nine to over 16 million. Fixture positions are schematic.
explanations.lobby marble columns: Marble columns in the three story lobby. Layout is schematic.
explanations.lobby marble walls: The lobby contains two tiers of marble: a wainscoting of darker marble, topped by lighter marble. Wall layout is schematic.
explanations.lobby ceiling slab: The ceiling slab of the three story lobby. The original ceilings held an Art Deco mural, shown as a separate part. Layout is schematic.
explanations.lobby terrazzo floor: A zigzagging terrazzo tile pattern crosses the lobby floor from east to west.
explanations.lobby ceiling mural: An Art Deco mural inspired by the sky and the Machine Age was installed in the lobby ceilings. Reproductions were installed after the originals were damaged.
explanations.lobby bronze motifs: Above each lobby doorway sits a bronze motif depicting one of three crafts used in construction: Electricity, Masonry, and Heating.
explanations.lobby information desk: The information desk in the Fifth Avenue lobby. A 2009 renovation replaced the clock over the desk with an anemometer.
explanations.lobby aluminum relief: An aluminum relief of the skyscraper as it was originally built, without the antenna, at the west end of the lobby, with rays radiating from the spire and the sun behind it. Shown schematically.
explanations.lobby revolving doors: The lobby entrance holds one set of double doors between a pair of revolving doors. Shown schematically.
explanations.lobby escalators: Escalators at the west ends of the north and south lobby walls lead to a mezzanine level. Shown schematically.
explanations.steel columns, floors 1 to 30: Riveted steel columns in the low range. The riveted steel frame was designed to handle all of the gravitational stresses and wind loads. Each floor is pierced by 210 structural columns; the grid shown is schematic.
explanations.steel columns, floors 31 to 71: Riveted steel columns in the middle range. Each floor is pierced by 210 structural columns; the grid shown is schematic.
explanations.steel columns, floors 72 to 86: Riveted steel columns in the high range. Each floor is pierced by 210 structural columns; the grid shown is schematic.
explanations.steel columns, crown tower: Riveted steel columns inside the crown tower. The grid shown is schematic.
explanations.central utility shaft: Utilities are grouped in a central shaft. On the 6th through 86th stories the shaft is surrounded by a main corridor on all four sides.
explanations.typical office floor plates: Typical office floor plates. The corridor is surrounded in turn by office space 28 feet (8.5 m) deep. Shown schematically.
explanations.setback level girder rings: Steel girders tie the frame at each setback level. The structure rates 42 pounds per square foot of structural stiffness.
explanations.crown tower girder rings: Steel girders tie the crown tower frame. Shown schematically.
explanations.express elevators, lobby to 80th floor: Four express elevators originally connected the lobby, the 80th floor, and landings in between. The original 64 elevators were built by the Otis Elevator Company.
explanations.low rise local elevators: Local elevators serve the low rise floors. Of the original 64 elevators, 54 were local cars for passengers. Bank arrangement is schematic.
explanations.mid rise local elevators: Local elevators serve the mid rise floors. The setbacks correspond to the tops of the elevator shafts. Bank arrangement is schematic.
explanations.high rise local elevators: Local elevators serve the high rise floors and the 86th floor observatory. Bank arrangement is schematic.
explanations.freight elevators: Eight of the original elevators were for freight deliveries. Shown schematically.
explanations.80th to 86th shuttle elevators: Additional elevators connect the 80th floor to the six floors above it, since the six extra floors were approved after the original 80 stories.
explanations.86th to 102nd observatory elevator: An elevator connects the 86th and 102nd floor observatories, and lets employees reach the mechanical floors between the 87th and 101st floors.
explanations.base east facade: Indiana limestone panels on the base east facade, made by the Indiana Limestone Company from stone quarried in south-central Indiana. The second through fourth stories alternate windows with wide stone piers and narrower mullions. Pier and window rhythm is schematic.
explanations.base west facade: Indiana limestone panels on the base west facade, made by the Indiana Limestone Company from stone quarried in south-central Indiana. The second through fourth stories alternate windows with wide stone piers and narrower mullions. Pier and window rhythm is schematic.
explanations.base north facade: Indiana limestone panels on the base north facade, made by the Indiana Limestone Company from stone quarried in south-central Indiana. The second through fourth stories alternate windows with wide stone piers and narrower mullions. Pier and window rhythm is schematic.
explanations.base south facade: Indiana limestone panels on the base south facade, made by the Indiana Limestone Company from stone quarried in south-central Indiana. The second through fourth stories alternate windows with wide stone piers and narrower mullions. Pier and window rhythm is schematic.
explanations.shaft core, floors 6 to 20: The structural core of the floors 6 to 20 run of the 81 story shaft. Interior office space is at most 28 feet (8.5 m) deep, ringing the central core. Setback widths are schematic.
explanations.limestone piers, floors 6 to 20: Indiana limestone piers on the floors 6 to 20 run. The tower bays are separated by alternating narrow and wide piers, a rhythm possibly influenced by the contemporary Daily News Building. Pier spacing is schematic.
explanations.window bays, floors 6 to 20: Window bays on the floors 6 to 20 run. The windows project slightly from the limestone cladding and are arranged in bays of one, two, or three per floor, separated by vertical nickel-chrome steel mullions within stainless steel frames. Window layout is schematic.
explanations.aluminum spandrels, floors 6 to 20: Horizontal aluminum spandrel bands between the floors of the floors 6 to 20 run. Using aluminum spandrels instead of stone avoided the need for cross-bonding. Band positions are schematic.
